# Chalk on a blackboard (`chalk`)

A teacher's pen writing on a dark slate, stroke by stroke: maths, graphs, equations, rates.

## Reference board

`demo-interest-chalk` in `fixtures/demos/boards/interest-chalk/` (`index.html`, `chalk.js`,
`graph.js`; no libraries). Compound interest on 1000: `rate` (1–15 %) and `years` (0–30) set a
straight simple-interest line and a compound curve; a marker at `years` shows the gap. Targets:
`#graph`, `#simple`, `#compound`, `#rate-control`, `#years-control`. `get_style` returns these
files: start new boards from this structure (`chalk.js` as is, a new drawing file in the shape
of `graph.js`, the same `onState`).

## Palette

| Role                                   | Hex                   |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Slate: body, `--nl-backdrop`, canvas   | `#1f2b27`             |
| Chalk: axes, arrows, panel text        | `#f4f1e8`             |
| First data line and its panel value    | `#cfe8ff`             |
| Second data line, slider accent        | `#ffe066`             |
| The key fact (the gap and its value)   | `#f48fb1`             |
| Dim chalk: ticks, units, formula       | `#93a39c`             |
| Faint full-range lines (blue / yellow) | `#5d6f68` / `#6f6a45` |
| Smudges, radial, alpha 0.025–0.06      | `rgba(220,230,225,…)` |

## Type

NL Sans only. Panel: title 44/600, values 34/600, formula 26, slider labels 28; portrait raises
labels and formula to 32. On the slate (canvas `fillText`): ticks 24–26, axis words 26, gap value
30 bold, the same in portrait. `board:check` measures only HTML text: draw canvas text at 32+
in portrait.

## Drawing technique

Canvas 2D, no library. One `<canvas id="graph">` plus two offscreen canvases of the same size: a
**chalk layer** and a **noise mask**. Per picture: `ch.board()` fills the slate and 26 smudges
from `lcg(3)`; every stroke and word goes on the layer; `ch.flush()` punches the noise out of the
layer and lays it on the slate. Each stroke is two passes, soft and wide under bright and narrow:

```js
for (const [width, alpha] of [
  [(o.width || 5) * 2.2, 0.18],
  [o.width || 5, 0.92],
]) {
  lg.strokeStyle = o.color || '#f4f1e8';
  lg.globalAlpha = alpha;
  lg.lineWidth = width;
  lg.lineCap = lg.lineJoin = 'round';
  // moveTo(pts[0]); lineTo the first ceil(pts.length * p) points; stroke()
}
```

No `Math.random`. Wobble is `sin()`: `curve(a, b, ctrl)` is a quadratic Bézier plus
`amp * Math.sin(u * 9)` (`amp = min(2, length / 80)`); data paths add `1.5 * Math.sin(i * 0.7)`
to x and `1.5 * Math.sin(i * 1.3)` to y. Texture is a seeded LCG, built once per size:

```js
const lcg = (seed) => () => (seed = (seed * 16807) % 2147483647) / 2147483647;
d[i + 3] = rnd() < 0.22 ? 150 + rnd() * 105 : 0; // noise mask from lcg(7), in resize()
// flush():
lg.globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-out';
lg.drawImage(noise, 0, 0);
lg.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over';
g.drawImage(layer, 0, 0);
lg.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
```

Also `arrow()` (heads ±2.6 rad, 20px), `write(str, x, y, p, o)` (uncovers text through a clip
rect in writing order, right to left for Arabic) and `dot()`. Widths: axes 4, ticks 3, faint
lines 2, data 6. The picture is redrawn from scratch on every state; the marker is drawn only at
`p === 1`, followed by a second `flush()`.

## Layout

- **Landscape 1280×720:** the canvas fills the board; graph at x 130–800, y 120–610; `.panel`
  absolute at the right, 400×720, padding 44/36, column gap 14.
- **Portrait 720×1280:** on a layout change `ch.resize(720, 1280)` and the canvas CSS size are
  set; graph at x 120–660, y 150–640; `.panel` at top 740, 720×540, values side by side. The
  layout comes from `env.layout` in `onState`; CSS switches on `[data-layout='portrait']`.

## Controls and states

- `<input type="range">` in a `<label>` grid (text above), width 100%, height 96,
  `accent-color: #ffe066`, `direction: ltr` even in Arabic, to run the way the x-axis does.
- Panel values take their line's colour, so highlighting `#simple` points at the blue line too.
  Numbers through `Intl.NumberFormat('ar-EG' | 'en')`.
- Highlight and notes are the helper's: 4px `#e0a526` outline, `#fff8e1` note boxes. The
  reference uses no `data-reveal`; to reveal a part, make it an HTML element with that attribute.

## Motion

- **Lesson moves on, input locked, state key changed** (`rate|years|layout|lang`): the pen draws
  the data lines over 1100 ms, eased `k * k * (3 - 2 * k)`, via `requestAnimationFrame`; axes and
  faint lines are there at once; the marker appears at the end.
- **Learner changes a slider (input open)** and **reduced motion:** instant `draw(1)`, the end
  picture. Always `cancelAnimationFrame(frame)` first.

## Do and don't

- Do draw every line twice, flush through the noise mask; wobble from `sin()`, texture from LCG.
- Do show context faint and the answer bright; one pink for the single key fact.
- Do keep sentences, numbers and controls in the HTML panel; the slate gets ticks and labels.
- Don't use `Math.random` or rebuild the noise per frame.
- Don't use pure black or white: slate `#1f2b27`, chalk `#f4f1e8`.
- Don't animate the learner's own changes or replay the pen when the key is unchanged.

## Before put_board

- `npm run board:check -- <folder>` passes: both layouts, Arabic and English.
- Text ≥24 landscape and ≥32 portrait (canvas text included), 8px from the edges.
- Sliders and buttons 96 high; the canvas is resized on layout change.
- Same state, same picture: no randomness; reduced motion and open input draw `p = 1`.
- `libraries: []`, classic `<script src>` files, `NewLearnBoard.observe` on every state.

watercolour.guide:
# Hand-painted watercolour (`watercolour`)

Warm, calm and handmade, like a picture-book page: nature, plants, food, home, health, daily life.

## Reference board

`demo-plants-painted` in `fixtures/demos/boards/plants-painted/` (`index.html`, `paint.js`,
`scene.js`; libraries `p5@2.3.3` and `p5.brush@2.2.3`). A window, a pot of basil on a table and a
magnified circle of the top 2 cm of soil. One choice variable, `soil`: `moist`, `dry` (pale soil,
cracks, drooping leaves), `watered` (can, stream, drops, water in the saucer). Targets: `#scene`,
`#probe`, `#choices`, `#verdict`. `get_style` returns these files: start new boards from this
structure (`paint.js` as is, a new `scene.js`, the same p5 setup and `onState`).

## Palette

| Role                                         | Hex                                        |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Paper: body, `--nl-backdrop`, `p.background` | `#f3ebdc`                                  |
| Ink outlines, panel text                     | `#2b2233`                                  |
| Hint text                                    | `#5b4b44`                                  |
| Cards (verdict, idle buttons)                | `#fff7ea`                                  |
| Terracotta: selected button, pot, border     | `#d97757`, `#c8663f`, `#a85a42`            |
| Leaf greens; stem                            | `#5e9a4e`, `#67a957`, `#a9b276`; `#3f6b37` |
| Water and sky                                | `#8ec3e6`, `#6fb2da`, `#3a9c98`, `#d7e8ef` |
| Earth and wood                               | `#4a3426`, `#b9946a`, `#c99a63`            |
| Grain vignette (multiplied)                  | `rgba(120,95,70,.28)`                      |

## Type

NL Sans, all in HTML: title 46/600 (line-height 1.2), hint and verdict inherit the body's 32,
choice buttons 28/600 (32 in portrait), the label under the magnifier 26/600 (34 in portrait).
The painting carries no text.

## Drawing technique

p5 in instance mode with p5.brush on a **WEBGL** canvas, 760×720, `pixelDensity(1)`, `noLoop()`:
the scene is painted once per state with `p.redraw()`. `draw()` sets the paper background and
translates by `(-BOX.w / 2, -BOX.h / 2)` so design coordinates start top left. Every element is
one `shape(points, opts)`: a flat `wash`, a watercolour `fill` (bleed 0.1, texture 0.4/0.35) and a
tapered outline with the custom `ink` brush; `line()` is an ink spline. Points come from `ell()`,
`rect()` and `leaf()`, jittered a little. Shapes are drawn round their own centre (`centred()`),
because p5.brush loses strokes far from the origin. Before each element, `key('name')` reseeds:

```js
const key = (k) => {
  let h = 2166136261 ^ seed;
  for (const c of String(k)) h = Math.imul(h ^ c.charCodeAt(0), 16777619);
  p.randomSeed(h >>> 0);
  p.noiseSeed(h >>> 0);
};
key('pot');
shape(potPoints, { wash: '#D97757', fill: '#C8663F', fillOp: 120, sw: 1.1 });
key('soil');
shape(ell(380, 378, 120, 17, 28, 1.5), { wash: s.soil, sw: 0.7 });
```

Options: `washOp` (255), `fillOp` (170), `ink: null` for no outline, `sw` stroke weight, `curv`
for curved vertices. Setup: `brush.scaleBrushes(3.2)` and `brush.add('ink', { weight: 5,
scatter: 0.25, sharpness: 0.8, grain: 40, opacity: 235, pressure: [1.15, 0.75], … })`. Each state
is a table of colours (`SOIL[soil]`: soil, top, leaf, droop) plus `if (soil === …)` extras.

Over the painting, a second 2D canvas `#grain` with `mix-blend-mode: multiply`: seeded LCG
paper speckle plus a radial vignette, made once. Labels and hit areas are HTML on top: `#probe`
is a round div placed over the painted magnifier from `PROBE {x, y, r}`, so it can be
highlighted. Before p5 loads, the board drops `devicemotion`/`deviceorientation` listeners,
which the sandbox forbids (copy that `<script>` as is).

## Layout

- **Landscape 1280×720:** `#scene` 760×720 at the left; `.panel` 520×720 at the right, padding
  56/48, column gap 22: title, hint, choice buttons, verdict.
- **Portrait 720×1280:** the same 760×720 painting, `transform: translate(0, 19px)
scale(0.9474)` so it is 720 wide; `.panel` at top 720, 720×560, padding 24/48/40.
- Keep **one painting size** for both layouts: p5.brush keeps its buffers at the first size.

## Controls and states

- Choice buttons rebuilt in `onState`: flex, `min-height: 96px`, `min-width: 120px`, 3px
  `#a85a42` border, uneven radius `22px 14px 24px 12px` (hand-cut), `#fff7ea` background; the
  chosen one `aria-pressed="true"`, `#d97757` with white text.
- `#verdict` is a `#fff7ea` card, radius 16, with an 8px `border-inline-start` whose colour
  follows `html[data-soil]`: green `#5e9a4e`, terracotta `#d97757`, teal `#3a9c98`.
- Highlight and notes are the helper's (4px `#e0a526` outline, `#fff8e1` notes); give a painted
  part an HTML overlay like `#probe` so it can be a target.

## Motion

None. A new state repaints the whole scene at once, whether the lesson or the learner changed
it, so reduced motion shows the same picture. A repaint takes about 3 s on software WebGL.

## Do and don't

- Do call `key('unique-name')` before every element; same key, same brushwork.
- Do paint once per state (`noLoop` + `redraw`): no animation loop, no "boiling" lines.
- Do keep labels, numbers and sentences in HTML; the painting has no text.
- Do use soft, warm colours from the table; no pure black (ink is `#2b2233`). White appears
  only as a translucent cloud wash and on the selected button's text.
- Do keep the multiplied grain canvas and the vignette; they make it read as paper.
- Don't use `Math.random`; jitter only through `p.random()` after `key()`.
- Don't change the canvas size between layouts; scale `#scene` with CSS.
- Don't draw strokes far from a shape's centre; go through `shape()` and `line()`.

## Before put_board

- `npm run board:check -- <folder>` passes: both layouts, Arabic and English, every option.
- HTML text ≥24 landscape and ≥32 portrait; buttons 96 high; 8px from the edges.
- Same state, same picture: a `key()` per element, grain from a fixed seed.
- `libraries: ["p5@2.3.3", "p5.brush@2.2.3"]`, loaded from `/lib/p5@2.3.3/lib/p5.min.js` and
  `/lib/p5.brush@2.2.3/dist/p5.brush.js` as classic scripts after the device-motion guard.
- `NewLearnBoard.start` runs from p5's `setup()`, after the canvas exists.

crt.guide:
# Green-phosphor terminal (`crt`)

An old computer screen glowing green in a dark bezel: technology, AI, data, code, numbers.

## Reference board

`demo-ai-crt` in `fixtures/demos/boards/ai-crt/` (`index.html`, `model.js`; no libraries). A toy
language model writes a sentence word by word: `words` (0–5) is how many are written,
`temperature` (0.2–2) reshapes the five candidates' chances (`p^(1/T)`); a fixed lottery number
per step picks the word. Targets: `#sentence`, `#bars`, `#temp-control`, `#next`, `#pick`.
`get_style` returns these files: start new boards from this structure (bezel, screen, two
columns, a pure `model.js` that turns state into data, one `onState` that rebuilds the DOM).

## Palette

| Role                                         | Hex / value                       |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Room: body, `--nl-backdrop`                  | `#11120f`                         |
| Bezel gradient (160deg), top edge highlight  | `#2b2a24` → `#171713`, `#3a3930`  |
| Screen (radial, centre → edge)               | `#0f2a18` → `#07150c` → `#040b06` |
| Phosphor `--ph`: text, bars, borders, slider | `#8dffa6`                         |
| Dim phosphor `--dim`: prompt line, bar frame | `#3f8f55`                         |
| Secondary text: percentages, pick sentence   | `#c9ffd5`                         |
| The answer: newest word, picked row          | `#e8ffb0`                         |
| Text glow (two shadows)                      | `rgb(141 255 166 / 65%)`, `/ 25%` |
| Scanlines                                    | `rgb(0 0 0 / 22%)`                |

## Type

NL Sans (no monospace font is allowed; the terminal feel comes from glow, `>` prompts and
blocks). Landscape: sentence 44/600 (line-height 1.35), candidate rows 32, percentages 28,
slider label 28, pick line 28, the command line 26, buttons the body's 32. Portrait: sentence 50,
rows 34, and percentages, label, pick and command line 32.

## Drawing technique

No canvas: everything is HTML and CSS, rebuilt from state in `onState`.

- `.bezel` (inset 14px, radius 34, padding 22) holds `.screen` (radius 26, `overflow: hidden`)
  with the radial gradient and two inset shadows: `0 0 70px rgb(0 0 0 / 70%)` for the curved
  dark edge and `0 0 18px rgb(141 255 166 / 18%)` for the inner glow.
- Scanlines are one pseudo-element over the screen; glow is a text-shadow on `.glow, .glow *`:

```css
.screen::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  pointer-events: none;
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, rgb(0 0 0 / 22%) 0 2px, transparent 2px 5px);
}
.glow,
.glow * {
  text-shadow:
    0 0 6px rgb(141 255 166 / 65%),
    0 0 18px rgb(141 255 166 / 25%);
}
```

- Bars are block segments: a 30px box with a 2px `--dim` border and 3px padding; the fill is
  `repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, var(--ph) 0 14px, transparent 14px 18px)`, its width set
  inline to the rounded percentage. Rows are a grid `150px 1fr 90px`: word, bar, percent.
- The command line is literal terminal text, LTR: `` `> next_word --temperature ${tf}` ``.
- A block cursor (22×40, `--ph`) ends the sentence and blinks with `steps(1)`.
- Determinism: no randomness at all. `model.js` uses fixed tables and `LOTTERY` numbers, so
  `generate(lang, words, temperature)` always returns the same sentence; temperature is rounded
  to one decimal before use.

## Layout

- **Landscape 1280×720:** bezel fills the board; `.screen` is a grid `1fr 330px`, gap 36,
  padding 30/40: left the prompt, sentence and bars; right `.side` (slider, two buttons, the
  pick sentence), centred vertically.
- **Portrait 720×1280:** `.screen` becomes one column (`grid-template-rows: auto 1fr`), padding
  30/32; rows widen to `170px 1fr 100px`; `.side` starts at the top.
- Only CSS switches the layout (`[data-layout='portrait']`); `onState` also sets
  `document.documentElement.dir` from `env.lang`.

## Controls and states

- Buttons: transparent, 3px `--ph` border, radius 10, phosphor text 600, `min-height: 88px`
  in the reference; new boards use 96. Labels carry arrows (`◀`/`▶`, `↺`).
- Slider: `accent-color: var(--ph)`, height 88 in the reference (use 96), `direction: ltr`.
- A step forward is a button that sets the next value (`words + 1`), not a hidden animation.
- The answer is marked in the look: newest word `#e8ffb0`, picked row `#e8ffb0` with `▶ `.
- Highlight and notes are the helper's (4px `#e0a526` outline, `#fff8e1` notes).

## Motion

Nothing moves between states except the blinking cursor: every state, from the lesson or the
learner, is rebuilt instantly. Reduced motion: the helper sets `data-reduced-motion`, which turns
CSS animations off, so the cursor stays lit: that is the end picture.

## Do and don't

- Do keep the bezel, curved dark screen, scanlines and text glow on every board of the course.
- Do draw quantities as segmented blocks with an exact percentage beside them.
- Do keep one bright accent (`#e8ffb0`) for the answer; the rest is phosphor and dim phosphor.
- Do write prompts and numbers like terminal output, left to right.
- Don't use `Math.random`; fixed tables or fixed lottery numbers stand in for chance.
- Don't fill with pure black or white; the darkest screen edge is `#040b06`.
- Don't add CSS transitions or animations other than the cursor blink.
- Don't add a monospace font; only NL Sans, NL Naskh and KaTeX are allowed.

## Before put_board

- `npm run board:check -- <folder>` passes: both layouts, Arabic and English.
- Text ≥24 landscape and ≥32 portrait, including the prompt line and percentages.
- Buttons and sliders 96 high (the reference's 88 is the bare minimum).
- Same state, same picture: no randomness; the cursor is not part of the state.
- `libraries: []`, classic `<script src>` files, `NewLearnBoard.observe` on every state.

space3d.guide:
# 3D space scene (`space3d`)

Bold, simple 3D forms in deep space that move as you watch: astronomy, planets, atoms, bodies.

## Reference board

`demo-seasons-3d` in `fixtures/demos/boards/seasons-3d/` (`index.html`, `space.js`, `sky.js`;
library `three@0.186.1`). The Sun, the orbit and the tilted Earth; `month` (1–12) moves the Earth
round the Sun, `tilt` (0–45°) tilts its axis; the panel shows Cairo's day length and noon Sun
height. Targets: `#space`, `#info`, `#month-control`, `#tilt-control`, `#season`. `get_style`
returns these files: start new boards from this structure (a pure maths file like `sky.js`, a
scene builder like `space.js`, the same inline module and `onState`).

## Palette

| Role                                      | Hex / value                                |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Space: body, `--nl-backdrop`, scene       | `#050816`                                  |
| Panel text                                | `#eef2ff`                                  |
| Accent: season, key numbers, slider, pole | `#ffd36e`                                  |
| Panel backing (landscape, fades leftward) | `rgb(10 16 48 / 92%)` → transparent        |
| Info card                                 | `rgb(255 255 255 / 7%)`, radius 16         |
| Stars; orbit line; label sprites          | `#c8d0ff`; `#3d4f96`; `#c9d4ff`            |
| Sun; its glow (radial)                    | `#ffcf5a`; `rgba(255,214,110,.95)` → 0     |
| Light: point; ambient                     | `#fff4dd` (3.2); `#8090ff` (0.3)           |
| Earth ocean; land cap; axis; equator      | `#2f6fd6`; `#3f9a6a`; `#e8ecff`; `#ffffff` |

## Type

NL Sans in the HTML panel: title 38/600, season 30/600, info lines 28 with values in `<b>`
(`#ffd36e`), slider labels 28; portrait raises season, info and labels to 32. In the scene, month
names are sprites drawn on a 256×80 canvas in `600 40px 'NL Sans'`; they are pictures, so the
checker does not measure them: keep them few and large.

## Drawing technique

three.js 0.186.1 in a WebGL renderer, `antialias: true`, `setPixelRatio(1)`, **rendered only on
demand** (no render loop). Load it from the one inline `<script type="module">`; keep your own
files classic scripts that take `THREE` as a parameter:

```js
import * as THREE from '/lib/three@0.186.1/build/three.module.js';
const space = buildSpace(THREE, $('space')); // space.js: function buildSpace(THREE, container)
NewLearnBoard.start({
  onState(view, env) {
    // …clamp variables, fill the panel, then:
    const animate = env?.reducedMotion !== true && view.input !== 'open';
    space.show({ month, tilt, layout, animate, labels: t.months });
  },
});
```

The scene, built once: 700 stars as `THREE.Points` (size 0.18) on a radius-60 sphere from an LCG
with seed 9; the Sun as `MeshBasicMaterial` (unlit) with a glow `Sprite` (scale 7) whose texture
is a canvas radial gradient; one `PointLight` (decay 0) and a blue `AmbientLight`; the orbit as a
128-segment `THREE.Line`. Lit bodies use `MeshStandardMaterial` (roughness 0.75–0.85). Thin
`TorusGeometry` rings mark lines on a body (equator, Cairo's latitude). Nesting does the physics:
`earth` group (position on the orbit) holds `tilted` group (`rotation.z = -tilt`), which holds
globe, axis cylinder, pole dot and rings. `place(angle, tilt)` is the only thing that changes per
state, then `renderer.render(scene, camera)`. Text sprites are rebuilt only when the language's
labels change. The maths lives in `sky.js` (pure functions of the variables), not in the scene.

## Layout

- **Landscape 1280×720:** `#space` 820×720 at the left, renderer `setSize(820, 720)`, camera
  `PerspectiveCamera(38)` at `(0, 8.5, 14.5)`; `.panel` 460×720 at the right, padding 30/36,
  gap 10, over a gradient that fades into space.
- **Portrait 720×1280:** `#space` 720×680, renderer resized, camera pulled back to
  `(0, 11.5, 17.5)`; `.panel` at top 680, 720×600, padding 20/44/36, no backing.
- Both cameras `lookAt(0, -0.8, 0)`; `show()` resets size, aspect and camera only when the
  layout changes.

## Controls and states

- `<input type="range">` in a `<label>` grid, width 100%, height 96, `accent-color: #ffd36e`,
  `direction: ltr`. The label names the value in words (`Month: June`, `Axis tilt: 23.5°`).
- Key numbers sit in the `#info` card in `#ffd36e` bold; the season line is the headline.
- Highlight and notes are the helper's (4px `#e0a526` outline, `#fff8e1` notes); `#space` is the
  whole 3D view as one target. Mark parts of the scene with accent colour, not with targets.

## Motion

- **Lesson moves on (input locked):** `show()` eases from the shown pose to the new one over
  1000 ms, `k * k * (3 - 2 * k)`; the orbit angle always goes forward (delta wrapped to 0–2π)
  and the tilt eases with it. `cancelAnimationFrame` first.
- **Learner drags (input open)** and the **first state:** placed and rendered at once.
- **Reduced motion:** `animate` is false, so the end pose is rendered straight away.

## Do and don't

- Do render on demand: one `render()` per state or per animation frame, never a loop.
- Do seed anything scattered (stars) with a fixed LCG; never `Math.random`.
- Do use groups for motion (position group → tilt group → parts), so one setter places it.
- Do use unlit materials for what glows and for markers; one warm light for the rest.
- Do drop true scale where it would hide the idea (the reference is not to scale).
- Don't put sentences in the 3D scene; the panel carries the words and numbers.
- Don't add camera drags: only three.module.js and three.core.js are served, no addons.
- Don't import three.js from your own files; only the inline module imports it.

## Before put_board

- `npm run board:check -- <folder>` passes: both layouts, Arabic and English.
- HTML text ≥24 landscape and ≥32 portrait; sliders 96 high; 8px from the edges.
- Same state, same picture: seeded stars, pose from state only, reduced motion renders the end.
- `libraries: ["three@0.186.1"]`, imported from `/lib/three@0.186.1/build/three.module.js`.
- Renderer and camera resized on layout change; nothing outside the 1280×720 / 720×1280 canvas.

seachart.guide:
# Sea chart (`demo-suez-map`)

An old nautical chart in brown ink on stained parchment, a pen drawing the route; for geography,
trade, history, journeys and anything that happens on a map.

## Reference board

`demo-suez-map`, folder `fixtures/demos/boards/suez-map/`: a ship from Singapore to Rotterdam
through Suez or round the Cape. Variables: `route` (choice `suez`/`cape`) and `speed` (number
10–22 knots, step 1). Targets: `#chart`, `#route-choice`, `#speed-control`, `#trip`, `#saving`.
`get_style` returns its files (`board.json`, `index.html`, `chart.js`, `coasts.js`); start a new
board from that structure: data file (shapes as `[lon, lat]`), drawing file, then `index.html`.

## Palette

| Role                                 | Value                                         |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| Parchment / panel / `--nl-backdrop`  | `#e9d8b0` / `#efe1bf` / `#d9c59a`             |
| Text ink / line ink (`INK`)          | `#3b2614` / `#5a3b22`                         |
| Land / inland seas                   | `#dcc595` / `#e4d3aa`                         |
| Coast water lines (3 strokes)        | `rgba(70,95,110,a)`, a = 0.05 / 0.07 / 0.10   |
| Paper stains                         | `rgba(150,105,55,a)`, a = 0.04–0.10           |
| Edge vignette                        | `rgba(110,70,30,a)`, a = 0 → 0.32             |
| Graticule / faint other route        | `rgba(90,59,34,0.18)` / `rgba(90,59,34,0.45)` |
| Accent: chosen route, ports, pressed | `#8e2a1a`, pressed text `#fff6e6`             |
| Compass points / ship hull / sail    | `#c9a46b` / `#7a2a18` / `#f4ead2`             |
| Button paper / place-label chip      | `#f6ecd2` / `rgb(240 226 192 / 85%)`          |
| Good-news line (`#saving`)           | `#2f5a3a`                                     |

## Type

NL Sans only (helper default `32px/1.4`; buttons inherit 32px). Landscape: title 38px 600,
labels and figures 28px, `.cartouche` 26px, place names 24px 600. Portrait raises labels,
figures, places and cartouche to 32px. No text is drawn on the `<canvas>`: every word is an HTML
element over it, so board:check can measure it and both languages render.

## Drawing technique

Canvas 2D (`#chart`), no library. `drawChart()` repaints everything each frame: parchment,
graticule, coasts (clipped to the map box), frame (`strokeRect` 3px `INK`), compass rose (16
alternating `INK`/`#c9a46b` points), faint other route, chosen route up to `p`, port dots, ship
at the pen tip. Paper stains use a seeded Park–Miller generator, so the same state gives the
same paper; the engraved water lining is each coast path stroked three times, wide and faint to
narrow and darker, before the land fill (`#dcc595`) and its 1.6px `INK` outline:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```js
let s = 11; const rnd = () => (s = (s * 16807) % 2147483647) / 2147483647;
for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) { // stains; a radial vignette goes over them
  const x = rnd() * w, y = rnd() * h, r = 60 + rnd() * 220;
  const gr = g.createRadialGradient(x, y, 0, x, y, r);
  gr.addColorStop(0, `rgba(150,105,55,${0.04 + rnd() * 0.06})`);
  gr.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(150,105,55,0)');
  g.fillStyle = gr; g.fillRect(x - r, y - r, 2 * r, 2 * r);
}
for (const [width, alpha] of [[22, 0.05], [14, 0.07], [7, 0.1]]) {
  g.strokeStyle = `rgba(70,95,110,${alpha})`; g.lineWidth = width; g.lineJoin = 'round';
  lands.forEach((pts) => (pathOf(g, pts), g.stroke()));
}
```

Routes are dashed (`setLineDash`): chosen `#8e2a1a` 4.5px `[14, 8]` round caps, other 2.5px
`[4, 8]`. `routeLine(g, pts, upTo, style)` walks the polyline to a length and returns the tip,
where `ship()` is drawn. `project(box)` maps lon/lat linearly into the map box, and the box keeps
the data's aspect (145° × 100°) so the land never stretches.

## Layout

Landscape: chart `#chart-wrap` 860×720 at left; panel 420×720 at right, padding 36px 34px, gap
14px, a `3px double #5a3b22` rule on its chart side (`border-inline-end`; the page stays
`dir="rtl"` in both languages). Portrait: chart 720×560 on top, panel 720×720 below, padding
24px 44px 36px, the double rule on top. CSS switches on `[data-layout='portrait']`; JS reads
`env.layout` and sets `canvas.width/height` (860×720 or 720×560) and the map box
(`{x:24,y:76,w:812,h:560}` or `{x:16,y:64,w:688,h:474}`). Place labels are spans at `P(lon,lat)`
plus a fixed offset, centred by `translate(-50%, 0)`, clamped 90px from the chart's sides.

## Controls and states

Choice: two `flex: 1` buttons, `min-height: 96px`, `3px solid #5a3b22`, radius 12px, paper
`#f6ecd2`; the chosen one (`aria-pressed="true"`) fills `#8e2a1a` with `#fff6e6` text. Slider:
native range, 96px tall, `direction: ltr`, `accent-color: #8e2a1a`, its value in the label.
Results sit in `#trip`, a `2px solid #5a3b22` box with radius 10px, numbers in `<b>`. Highlight
and notes are the helper's defaults (outline `4px #e0a526`, note `#fff8e1`); the lessons use
`highlight` only.

## Motion

When the lesson brings a new route (or layout or language), the pen draws it over 1.6 s with
smoothstep easing and the ship rides the tip (`requestAnimationFrame`). A speed change, open
input or reduced motion draws `p = 1` at once. End picture: full route, ship at the destination.

```js
const key = `${route}|${layout}|${lang}`;
const animate = env?.reducedMotion !== true && view.input !== 'open' && key !== last;
last = key;
cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
if (!animate) return draw(1);
```

## Do and don't

- Do keep line work in `INK` `#5a3b22` and one red accent `#8e2a1a` for what the learner chose.
- Do keep randomness seeded and repaint the whole canvas every frame.
- Do put words in HTML labels over the canvas, on a parchment chip.
- Do show the alternative faint and dashed so the comparison stays visible.
- Don't use `Math.random()`, bright colours, gradients on land, or drop shadows.
- Don't animate slider changes or open input; only a new lesson choice animates.
- Don't draw text with `fillText`; it escapes the size, font and edge checks.

## Before put_board

- `npm run board:check -- <folder>` passes (it covers landscape, portrait, Arabic, English).
- Text ≥ 24px landscape, ≥ 32px portrait, place labels ≥ 8px from the edge; controls 96px.
- Same state, same picture: seeded paper; reduced motion draws `p = 1`.
- `libraries: []` as in the reference; classic `<script src>` files after the helper, no modules.
- Every id in `targets` exists in both layouts; `observe` is called on every state.

shadow.guide:
# Shadow puppets (`demo-pyramid-shadow`)

Flat dark silhouettes on cut-paper layers against a sunset sky; for history, crafts, work and
forces, stories of people doing things, any scene that reads well in profile.

## Reference board

`demo-pyramid-shadow`, folder `fixtures/demos/boards/pyramid-shadow/`: a 2.5-tonne block hauled
up a ramp on a sledge. Variables: `slope` (number 4–20°, step 1) and `sand` (choice
`dry`/`wet`). Targets: `#scene`, `#slope-control`, `#sand-choice`, `#ramp`, `#workers` (the last
two are the panel's figure lines, not SVG shapes). `get_style` returns its files (`board.json`,
`index.html`, `scene.js`, `physics.js`); start a new board from that structure: a model file
that returns numbers, a scene file that returns SVG markup, and `index.html`.

## Palette

| Role                                                | Value                                |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Silhouettes, ramp, text, backdrop (`--nl-backdrop`) | `#2b1b10`                            |
| Panel paper (body)                                  | `#f6e3c4`                            |
| Sky gradient top / middle / bottom                  | `#ffcf8a` / `#f4945a` / `#d9603f`    |
| Sun (opacity 0.92) / dune layer                     | `#ffe7b3` / `#eaa45c`                |
| Pyramid shaded / lit face / courses (opacity 0.6)   | `#b8622e` / `#cf8247` / `#8f4a20`    |
| Ground layer, slider accent / ramp struts           | `#9a5226` / `#5b3a22`                |
| Paper drop shadow                                   | `#4a1e08` at 0.45                    |
| Water drops (wet state only)                        | `#7fb7d8`                            |
| Figures box: background / text / numbers            | `#2b1b10` / `#ffe7b3` / `#ffb366`    |
| Choice button / pressed                             | `#fff3df` / `#2b1b10` with `#ffe7b3` |

## Type

NL Sans only (helper default `32px/1.4`; buttons inherit 32px). Landscape: title 40px 600,
figures 30px, note 28px (line-height 1.45), slider label 28px. Portrait: figures, note and label
32px. The scene has no text, so the SVG's scaling never shrinks words.

## Drawing technique

Inline SVG (`<svg id="scene" viewBox="0 0 860 720">`), no library. `sceneSvg(state)` returns the
whole scene as a string and `onState` sets `innerHTML`: each state is a full redraw. Back to
front: sky gradient, sun, dune, pyramid (two faces plus course lines), ground, ramp with struts,
block on its sledge with rope and crew, water if wet, then a paper grain over everything, all
clipped to the frame. Each paper layer gets the same soft drop shadow, which makes it cut paper:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```html
<filter id="lift" x="-10%" y="-10%" width="120%" height="130%">
  <feDropShadow dx="0" dy="5" stdDeviation="5" flood-color="#4a1e08" flood-opacity="0.45"/>
</filter>
<filter id="paper"><feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="0.9" numOctaves="2" seed="4"/>
  <feColorMatrix values="0 0 0 0 0.3  0 0 0 0 0.15  0 0 0 0 0.05  0 0 0 0.09 0"/></filter>
<!-- last child of the scene: -->
<rect width="860" height="720" filter="url(#paper)" opacity="1"/>
```

The grain is brown noise at alpha 0.09; the fixed `seed="4"` keeps it identical every draw.
Figures are flat `#2b1b10` paths (inherited `fill`) with no outline, placed and tilted by
`transform`; small per-index variation keeps a crowd from looking stamped, without randomness:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```js
const worker = (x, y, a, i) =>
  `<g transform="translate(${x} ${y}) rotate(${a}) scale(${i % 3 === 1 ? 0.95 : 1})">
     <circle cx="${i % 2 ? 1 : -1}" cy="-34" r="6"/>
     <path d="M2,-28 L-7,-8 L-12,10 L-7,10 L-2,-3 L3,10 L8,10 L4,-8 L5,-26 Z"/>
     <path d="M3,-22 L-14,-14 L-13,-11 L3,-17 Z"/>
   </g>`;
```

Geometry comes from the variables: the ramp foot is `TOP.x - (GROUND - TOP.y) / tan(slope)`,
`along(t)` gives a point on the ramp, workers are spaced along it and rotated by `-slope`. The
crew drawn is capped at 14 and the block kept on screen at gentle slopes; the panel shows the
true count.

## Layout

Landscape: scene 860×720 at left; panel 420×720 at right, padding 36px 34px, gap 14px: title,
figures box, note, slider, choice. Portrait: scene 720×603 on top (the same viewBox scaled by
720/860, so one drawing serves both), panel 720×677 below, padding 20px 44px 32px, gap 12px.
Only CSS changes, on `[data-layout='portrait']`.

## Controls and states

Choice: two `flex: 1` buttons, `min-height: 96px`, `3px solid #2b1b10`, radius 14px, paper
`#fff3df`; pressed (`aria-pressed="true"`) turns silhouette-dark `#2b1b10` with `#ffe7b3` text.
Slider: native range, 96px tall, `direction: ltr`, `accent-color: #9a5226`, value in the label.
Results: a dark box (radius 14px) like a lit puppet screen, numbers in `#ffb366`. Highlight and
notes are the helper's defaults (outline `4px #e0a526`, note `#fff8e1`); the lessons use
`highlight` only.

## Motion

None in the reference: every state, from the lesson or the learner, is an instant full redraw,
so reduced motion shows the same picture. Rebuilding with `innerHTML` makes new elements, so CSS
transitions would not run. If motion is added, use CSS animations (the helper's
`[data-reduced-motion] * { animation: none !important }` stops them) and make the resting frame
the state's true picture.

## Do and don't

- Do keep figures as flat `#2b1b10` silhouettes in profile: no outlines, no inner detail.
- Do stack paper layers, each with `filter="url(#lift)"`, warm colours darkening downward.
- Do finish with the `#paper` grain rect over the whole scene, `seed` fixed.
- Do derive every position from the variables with plain geometry.
- Do cap crowds to what fits and print the real number in the panel.
- Don't use `Math.random()`, cold colours (beyond a small water accent) or strokes on figures.
- Don't put text inside the SVG; keep words in the panel.
- Don't give SVG shapes the target ids `#ramp`/`#workers`: they belong to the panel lines.

## Before put_board

- `npm run board:check -- <folder>` passes (landscape, portrait, Arabic, English).
- Text ≥ 24px landscape, ≥ 32px portrait, ≥ 8px from the edge; controls 96px.
- Same state, same picture: fixed `seed`, no clocks or randomness in `sceneSvg`.
- `libraries: []` as in the reference; classic `<script src>` files after the helper, no modules.
- Every id in `targets` exists and is unique across SVG and panel; `observe` on every state.

blueprint.guide:
# Blueprint (`demo-circuit-blueprint`)

White technical lines on a gridded blue sheet with one warm yellow for what flows; for circuits,
machines, mechanics, engineering, plans and any labelled schematic.

## Reference board

`demo-circuit-blueprint`, folder `fixtures/demos/boards/circuit-blueprint/`: battery, switch,
resistor and a 6 Ω bulb in series. Variables: `switch` (choice `open`/`closed`), `volts` (number
1.5–9 V, step 1.5) and `resistor` (number 0–24 Ω, step 2). Targets: `#drawing`, `#bulb`,
`#meters`, `#switch-control`, `#volts-control`, `#resistor-control`. `get_style` returns its files
(`board.json`, `index.html`, `drawing.js`); start a new board from that structure: a drawing
file with the model and an SVG-string function, and `index.html` with styles and text.

## Palette

| Role                                     | Value                                              |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Body and panel / `--nl-backdrop`         | `#0e2d55` / `#0b2546`                              |
| Drawing sheet                            | `#123a6b`                                          |
| Lines, symbols, SVG labels / panel text  | `#f2f7ff` / `#e8f1ff`                              |
| Grid every 20 / every 100                | `rgb(255 255 255 / 7%)` / `rgb(255 255 255 / 15%)` |
| Accent: current, numbers, switch, slider | `#ffe066`                                          |
| Bulb halo centre / edge                  | `#fff4b8` / `#ffd23f`                              |
| Lit bulb fill                            | `rgba(255,236,150, 0.25 + 0.6·glow)`               |
| Formula line (`.law`)                    | `#a9c4ea`                                          |

## Type

NL Sans only (helper default `32px/1.4`; the switch button inherits 32px). Panel: title 40px
600; meters, formula and slider labels 28px landscape, 32px portrait. SVG labels `.t` 28px and
title block `.t.b` 26px in landscape; portrait raises them to 40px and 34px because the SVG is
scaled by 720/860 there, and board:check measures SVG text by its rendered height. The formula
`I = V ÷ R` is `direction: ltr` with `text-align: right`.

## Drawing technique

Inline SVG (`<svg id="drawing" viewBox="0 0 860 720">`), no library. `drawingSvg(state)` returns
the whole sheet as a string, set with `innerHTML` on every state. Styles live in CSS classes in
`index.html`, not in the markup: `.g`/`.G` grid, `.w` white line (4px, round caps, no fill),
`.w.thick` 9px, `.frame` 3px, `.dot` terminals, `.t` labels, `.flow` current. Order: sheet rect,
grid, frame inset 30px, wires, flow, symbols, halo, bulb, labels, title block.

```js
for (let x = 0; x <= 860; x += 20)
  grid.push(`<line x1="${x}" y1="0" x2="${x}" y2="720" class="${x % 100 ? 'g' : 'G'}"/>`);
for (let y = 0; y <= 720; y += 20)
  grid.push(`<line x1="0" y1="${y}" x2="860" y2="${y}" class="${y % 100 ? 'g' : 'G'}"/>`);
```

Parts are textbook schematic symbols built from the state: a long thin and a short thick line
per 1.5 V cell, a zigzag `polyline` resistor (a straight wire at 0 Ω), a switch arm level when
closed and tilted when open, a crossed circle for the bulb, a title block bottom right (`rect`
290×80, "Sheet 7 · Ohm's law"). Current is a dotted yellow path over the wires, its dashes slid
by CSS, faster as the bulb glows brighter:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```css
#drawing .flow { fill: none; stroke: #ffe066; stroke-width: 5; stroke-linecap: round;
  stroke-dasharray: 2 26; animation: flow linear infinite; }
@keyframes flow { to { stroke-dashoffset: -28; } }
/* per state, on the path: */
style="animation-duration:${(2.4 / Math.max(0.15, glow + 0.15)).toFixed(2)}s"
```

Brightness `glow = min(1, sqrt(I²·6 / 13.5))` sets the halo radius (`70 + 50·glow`), its stop
opacity and the bulb fill. No randomness anywhere.

## Layout

Landscape: drawing 860×720 at left; panel 420×720 at right (no own background), padding 32px
34px, gap 12px: title, `#meters`, formula, switch, two sliders. Portrait: drawing 720×603 on top
(same viewBox, scaled), panel 720×677 below, padding 16px 44px 28px, gap 10px. `#bulb` is an
empty round HTML div laid over the bulb symbol so the lesson can highlight it: 120×120 at
(670, 270) landscape, 100×100 at (561, 226) portrait (the symbol's centre × 720/860).

## Controls and states

The switch is one toggle button, not two choices: `min-height: 96px`, transparent, `3px solid
#ffe066`, radius 12px, yellow text naming the action ("Close the circuit" / "Open the
circuit"). Sliders: native range, 96px tall, `direction: ltr`, `accent-color: #ffe066`, value in
the label. `#meters` is a square-cornered `2px solid #f2f7ff` box, numbers in yellow `<b>`.
Highlight and notes are the helper's defaults (outline `4px #e0a526`, note `#fff8e1`); the
lessons use `highlight` only.

## Motion

Lesson steps and learner changes are both instant redraws (switch arm, cells, zigzag, glow).
The only motion is the looping current while the circuit is closed. Under reduced motion the
helper's `[data-reduced-motion] * { animation: none !important }` stops it at offset 0: the end
picture is the lit circuit with still dots on the wires.

## Do and don't

- Do draw everything in `#f2f7ff` lines on `#123a6b`, with the 20/100 grid and a 30px frame.
- Do keep yellow `#ffe066` for the one thing that flows or matters, and its numbers.
- Do use standard schematic symbols with short labels, plus a title block.
- Do keep line styles in CSS classes and `drawingSvg` pure (state in, string out).
- Do add an HTML overlay div for any SVG part the lesson must highlight, placed per layout.
- Do raise SVG font sizes in portrait so their scaled height stays ≥ 32px.
- Don't use fills, gradients or shadows on parts; only the bulb halo glows.
- Don't drive the current with JS timers; a CSS animation stops under reduced motion.

## Before put_board

- `npm run board:check -- <folder>` passes (landscape, portrait, Arabic, English).
- Text ≥ 24px landscape, ≥ 32px portrait (SVG labels after scaling); controls 96px.
- Same state, same picture: no randomness, motion only in CSS animations.
- `libraries: []` as in the reference; classic `<script src>` files after the helper, no modules.
- Every id in `targets` exists in both layouts and overlays line up; `observe` on every state.

crayon.guide:
# Crayon picture book (`crayon`)

Bright crayon on cream paper, wobbly and friendly: for children and first concepts (counting,
fractions, shapes, simple science), with big shapes and a few big words.

## Reference board

`demo-fractions-crayon` in `fixtures/demos/boards/fractions-crayon/` (`board.json`,
`index.html`, `pizza.js`). A pizza cut into `slices` (2–12) with `taken` (0–12) slices shaded
and slid out, beside a half pizza; a big `<`, `=` or `>` compares them. Targets: `#pizza`,
`#half`, `#fraction`, `#compare`, `#slices-control`, `#taken-control`. `libraries` is `[]`.
`get_style` returns these files: start a new board from their structure (an SVG string
builder in its own classic script, HTML text and controls in `index.html`) and change the topic.

## Palette

| Role                                     | Hex                   |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Paper (body, SVG background)             | `#fff8e6`             |
| Panel, `--nl-backdrop`                   | `#fff1d0`             |
| Ink text, fraction bar                   | `#3a2a1a`             |
| Outline crayon, title, tags              | `#c0392b`             |
| Red crayon: fraction, dots, hatch, range | `#e0533d`             |
| Shaded (taken) fill / plain fill         | `#ffb347` / `#ffe08a` |
| Crust fill / crust outline               | `#e9a84a` / `#a0522d` |
| Yellow: star doodle, dashed panel border | `#f4c430`             |
| Blue: sign, compare line, second hatch   | `#3d7be0`             |
| Doodles: mint, light blue                | `#7fc8a9`, `#9fb8ff`  |

Paper grain is not a hex: an `feColorMatrix` tints noise brown (0.55, 0.4, 0.2) at alpha 0.16.

## Type

NL Sans only (the helper's default, 32px/1.4); weight 600 for everything that matters.
Landscape: title 42, the fraction 64 (line-height 1), the sign 96, tags 28, compare 30,
slider labels 28. Portrait: tags 38, compare and labels 32; title, fraction and sign unchanged.
Numbers use `Intl.NumberFormat('ar-EG' | 'en')` (Arabic-Indic digits in Arabic). The fraction
is HTML, not SVG text: numerator, a 110×7px rounded bar, denominator in a grid.

## Drawing technique

One inline SVG (`viewBox 0 0 860 720`) rebuilt as a string on every state. Three signatures:

1. **Wobble**: every shape group sits under `filter="url(#crayon)"`, turbulence displacing the
   edges. Strokes are thick (5px), `stroke-linejoin`/`linecap: round`, red outline on yellow.
2. **Hatching**: shaded parts get a second path filled with a rotated line `<pattern>`
   (35° red, −35° blue), ids suffixed per shape (`hatch-a`, `hatch-b`).
3. **Grain**: a last full-size `<rect filter="url(#grain)">` lays fine noise over all.

```svg
<filter id="crayon"><feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="0.035"
    numOctaves="2" seed="5" result="n"/>
  <feDisplacementMap in="SourceGraphic" in2="n" scale="7"/></filter>
<filter id="grain"><feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="1.1" numOctaves="1" seed="2"/>
  <feColorMatrix values="0 0 0 0 0.55  0 0 0 0 0.4  0 0 0 0 0.2  0 0 0 0.16 0"/></filter>
<pattern id="hatch-a" width="14" height="14" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"
    patternTransform="rotate(35)">
  <line x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="14" stroke="#e0533d" stroke-width="4" opacity="0.55"/></pattern>
```

Randomness is fixed: turbulence has a `seed`, there is no `Math.random`. Decorations come
from the values (dots at fixed fractions of the radius on each slice's middle angle; a shaded
slice slides out `r * 0.09` on that angle). Doodles are fixed corner paths. Targets are empty
`<div>`s over the shapes with `border-radius: 50%`, so the helper's outline hugs the circle.

```js
const out = i < taken ? r * 0.09 : 0;
const [dx, dy] = [Math.cos(mid) * out, Math.sin(mid) * out];
parts.push(`<path d="${slicePath(cx + dx, cy + dy, r, a0, a1)}"
  fill="${i < taken ? '#ffb347' : '#ffe08a'}" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="5"/>`);
```

## Layout

Landscape 1280×720: the art (`#art`, 860×720) on the left; a 420px panel on the right
(`#fff1d0`, padding 34, column with 12px gaps) with a 6px dashed `#f4c430` divider
(`border-inline-end`, which lands on the left because the page is `dir="rtl"`).
Portrait 720×1280: `#art` is scaled by `0.8372` from the top-left (860 → 720 wide, 603 tall);
the panel moves to `top: 603px`, 720×677, with the dashed border on top. Switching is pure CSS
on `[data-layout='portrait']`; the SVG is the same in both.

## Controls and states

Native `<input type="range">` at `height: 96px`, full panel width, `accent-color: #e0533d`,
`direction: ltr` in both languages; each inside a `<label>` whose text states the value
("Taken: 3 slices"). `onState` writes the values back and caps `taken.max` at `slices`.
Highlight, reveal and notes come from the helper unchanged: a 4px `#e0a526` outline, hidden
`[data-reveal]` until revealed, and a `#fff8e1` note bubble at 32px. The reference uses no
`data-reveal`; add it to an element whose id is in `targets` if a step must reveal it.

## Motion

The reference has none: each state replaces the SVG `innerHTML` at once, so a drag is instant
and reduced motion already shows the end picture ("sliding out" is a static offset). To animate
a lesson step (`view.step` changed), use CSS only, which the helper turns off under
`[data-reduced-motion]`, and end on exactly the state's picture.

## Do and don't

- Do use one or two big objects that fill the art (the pizza has radius 220 in 860×720).
- Do use short, spoken words ("Taken: 3 slices", "Exactly a half!"), one idea per line.
- Do show the number beside the picture, large (64–96px) and in the learner's digits.
- Do keep thick round-capped strokes, flat fills, hatching for "this part".
- Do suffix every repeated pattern id per shape, and keep the turbulence seeds fixed.
- Don't put text inside the SVG; labels, tags and the sign are HTML over it.
- Don't use thin lines, gradients, shadows or more than a few doodles: they compete.
- Don't use `Math.random`, time or animation-frame state to draw.

## Before put_board

- `npm run board:check -- <folder>` passes: landscape and portrait, Arabic and English.
- Text ≥ 24px landscape, ≥ 32px portrait **after** the `0.8372` scale of `#art`: the check
  reads the CSS size, so size text inside `#art` at 40px or more in portrait (38 is borderline).
- Every control ≥ 88px on its short side (use 96); sliders stay `direction: ltr`.
- Same state ⇒ same SVG string: seeds fixed, no random, values clamped and rounded first.
- `libraries: []`, classic `<script src>` files (no modules), and `NewLearnBoard.observe` called.

calligraphy.guide:
# Arabic calligraphy and ink (`calligraphy`)

Calm black ink and large naskh on warm paper, with red and blue marking roles: for Arabic
grammar, spelling, poetry and Quran-style text, where the words themselves are the picture.

## Reference board

`demo-grammar-ink` in `fixtures/demos/boards/grammar-ink/` (`board.json`, `index.html`,
`ink.js`). «كَتَبَ الطالبُ الدرسَ» in large naskh with tags under each word, a meaning line,
and an ink drawing of who writes on whom. Variables: `doer` (`student` | `lesson`) swaps the
case endings and the picture; `order` (`vso` | `vos`) swaps the nouns but not the meaning.
Targets: `#sentence`, `#meaning`, `#picture`, `#doer-choice`, `#order-choice`, `#key`.
`libraries: ["amiri@5.3.0"]`. `get_style` returns these files: start a new board from their
structure (words built as DOM in `index.html`, the SVG drawing in its own classic script).

## Palette

| Role                                        | Hex       |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| Paper (body)                                | `#f6efe2` |
| `--nl-backdrop`                             | `#ece2cf` |
| Ink: text, strokes, borders, pressed button | `#1e1a16` |
| Red: doer ending and tag, pen nib, arrow    | `#b23a2a` |
| Blue: done-to ending and tag                | `#2a5ab2` |
| Muted brown: verb tag                       | `#6b5a48` |
| Light paper: buttons, notebook fill         | `#fbf6ea` |

The paper has two faint ink blots: `radial-gradient`s of `rgb(30 26 22 / 6%)` at 20% 30% and
`/ 7%` at 70% 75%, over `#f6efe2`. Red and blue mean the two roles everywhere: in the ending,
its tag, and the key in the panel.

## Type

- Display Arabic: `font-family: 'NL Naskh', serif` (Amiri, served by the helper from
  `amiri@5.3.0`), weight 700, 104px landscape / 88px portrait, `line-height: 1.5` so the
  harakat above and below are not clipped.
- Everything else is NL Sans: title 42/600, tags 26/600 (pill: 3px `currentColor` border,
  `border-radius: 999px`), meaning 32/600, key 26 with line-height 1.45, buttons 26/600.
  Portrait raises tags, key and buttons to 32 and the meaning to 34.
- Harakat are typed in the text (`'كَتَبَ'`). The case ending is the last letter plus its mark
  in its own `<span class="end doer|done">` inside the same `<b>`, so only it changes colour
  and the word stays one run. A mark shown alone sits on a tatweel: `( ـُ )`, `( ـَ )`.

```js
const WORDS = {
  verb: ['كَتَبَ', ''],
  student: ['الطال', { doer: 'بُ', done: 'بَ' }],
  lesson: ['الدر', { doer: 'سُ', done: 'سَ' }],
};
const [stem, ends] = WORDS[key];
b.append(stem);
const end = document.createElement('span');
end.className = `end ${role}`; // .end.doer red, .end.done blue
end.textContent = ends[role];
```

## Drawing technique

Text is HTML (a flex row of `.word` columns: the word, then its tag), rebuilt with
`replaceChildren` on each state. The flex row follows `dir="rtl"`, so the verb is rightmost.
The picture is an inline `<svg id="picture" viewBox="0 0 760 300">` whose `innerHTML` is set
from `pictureSvg(doer)`: simple line figures (a stick student, a lined notebook, a pen) built
by small functions with `translate(x y) scale(s)`, ink stroke 5px, round caps, paper fills.
The doer stands on the right (read first) and a red dashed arrow (`stroke-dasharray="14 10"`)
runs to the one written on. All of it sits under one mild ink-bleed filter with a fixed seed;
there is no randomness, so the picture depends only on `doer`:

```svg
<filter id="bleed"><feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="0.05" numOctaves="2"
  seed="7"/><feDisplacementMap in="SourceGraphic" scale="4"/></filter>
<g filter="url(#bleed)"> ...figures, pen, arrow... </g>
```

## Layout

Landscape 1280×720: `.page` (860×720) on the left holds the sentence (top 56, 34px gaps),
the meaning (top 330) and the picture (760×300 at 50, 400). A 420px panel on the right
(padding 36/34, 14px gaps) holds the title, the colour key and two rows of choices; a 3px
solid ink line divides them (`border-inline-end`, on the left because the page is RTL).
Portrait 720×1280: `.page` becomes 720×660 (sentence top 30, 18px gaps; meaning top 280;
picture 720×284 at top 360), and the panel moves to `top: 660px`, 720×620, ink line on top.
All of it is CSS on `[data-layout='portrait']`; nothing is scaled with `transform`.

## Controls and states

Each choice variable is a `.choices` row of `<button>`s (flex 1, `min-height: 96px`, 3px ink
border, radius 10, `#fbf6ea`), rebuilt each state with `aria-pressed` on the current value,
which inverts to ink with `#f6efe2` text; `onclick` calls `NewLearnBoard.setVariables`.
Highlight, reveal and notes are the helper's own: a 4px `#e0a526` outline, `[data-reveal]`
hidden until revealed (unused here), and a `#fff8e1` note at 32px. Highlight a whole word
group (`#sentence`) or the key, not a letter.

## Motion

None in the reference: each state rebuilds the words and sets the SVG at once, so a choice
flips the endings instantly and reduced motion is already the end picture. If a lesson step
(`view.step` changed) animates, use CSS only (the helper disables it under
`[data-reduced-motion]`) and finish on the state's picture.

## Do and don't

- Do make the Arabic the hero: one sentence or verse, 88–104px naskh, lots of paper around it.
- Do write the full harakat in the strings and keep `line-height` ≥ 1.5 on naskh.
- Do colour a grammatical role the same everywhere (ending, tag, key), with red and blue only.
- Do keep the drawing to a few ink line figures, 5px strokes, under the one bleed filter.
- Do put explanations in NL Sans and only display Arabic in NL Naskh.
- Don't split a word into separate boxes or add spacing inside it; colour the ending in a span.
- Don't draw Arabic as SVG `<text>` or images; keep it HTML so shaping and the check work.
- Don't add bright fills, gradients on shapes, or a third accent colour.

## Before put_board

- `npm run board:check -- <folder>` passes: landscape and portrait, Arabic and English.
- Text ≥ 24px landscape and ≥ 32px portrait (tags, key and buttons go up to 32 in portrait).
- Buttons `min-height: 96px`; the naskh line is not clipped at the top or bottom.
- Same state ⇒ same words and SVG: values normalised first, filter seed fixed, no random.
- `libraries: ["amiri@5.3.0"]` as in the reference; classic `<script src>`, no modules.

pixel.guide:
# Pixel game (`pixel`)

A retro pixel-art game on dark purple, with chunky square buttons: for programming, logic,
puzzles and step-by-step rules, where the learner builds moves and watches what happens.

## Reference board

`demo-robot-pixel` in `fixtures/demos/boards/robot-pixel/` (`board.json`, `index.html`,
`game.js`). A 7×5 maze: a program of six slots `c1`–`c6` (`none` | `up` | `down` | `left` |
`right`), repeated `repeat` (1–3) times, walks a robot towards a battery; a wall stops it.
Targets: `#maze`, `#program`, `#repeat-choice`, `#status`. `libraries` is `[]`. `get_style`
returns these files: start a new board from their structure (pure game logic and drawing in
`game.js`, text and buttons in `index.html`) and swap in the new puzzle.

## Palette

| Role                                            | Hex                   |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Background, `--nl-backdrop`, robot eyes (`c`)   | `#1b1035`             |
| Floor / button fill                             | `#2a1f4a`             |
| Floor checker                                   | `#33275a`, `#30245a`  |
| Wall / wall brick lines                         | `#5b3fa0` / `#7d5fd0` |
| Cyan: maze frame, move buttons, robot body (b)  | `#7cf2ff`             |
| Pink: robot antenna (a), wall bump, wall status | `#ff5d8f`             |
| Yellow: title, trail, repeat buttons, (d), (f)  | `#ffd166`             |
| Green: battery (g), goal sparks, goal status    | `#06d6a0`             |
| Robot legs (e) / battery cells (h)              | `#4cc9f0` / `#b8ffe9` |
| Text / hint and waiting status                  | `#e9f9ff` / `#b9a8ff` |
| Empty slot (`none`) text and border             | `#5b4f86`             |

Letters in brackets are the sprite palette keys in `game.js` (`PAL`).

## Type

NL Sans only; no text is drawn on the canvas. Landscape: title 38/600 in yellow, hint 26,
move arrows 44/600 (`·` `↑` `↓` `←` `→`), repeat buttons 32, status 28/600. Portrait raises the
hint and status to 32; the rest already meet it. Arrows are characters, so they need no
translation; each move button gets an `aria-label` with the move's name.

## Drawing technique

A tiny `<canvas id="maze" width="128" height="96">` is drawn with `fillRect` only and scaled
up by CSS with `image-rendering: pixelated` (832×624 landscape, 6.5×; 660×495 portrait). The
grid is 16px tiles at an 8px margin. Walls are a fill plus 1–2px lighter lines for bricks;
floors alternate two near shades. Sprites are 8×8 string grids, one character per pixel,
`.` transparent, each other character a key into `PAL`:

```js
const ROBOT = [
  '..aaaa..',
  '.abbbba.',
  '.bcbbcb.',
  '.bbbbbb.',
  '..bddb..',
  '.eeeeee.',
  '.e.ee.e.',
  '..e..e..',
];
```

```js
const sprite = (g, rows, x, y, s) =>
  rows.forEach((row, j) =>
    [...row].forEach((c, i) => {
      if (c === '.') return;
      g.fillStyle = PAL[c];
      g.fillRect(x + i * s, y + j * s, s, s);
    }),
  );
```

Each state redraws the whole frame in a fixed order: background, tiles, trail (4×4 yellow
dots on visited cells), battery (hidden once reached), robot at its last cell, then an
end effect (a pink X of 2×2 squares on the wall it bumped, or five green sparks at the goal).
The outcome comes from a pure `run(program, repeat)` that returns `{ path, end, bump, moves }`
with `end` one of `goal`, `wall`, `short`, `empty`; the drawing, status and observation all
read that one result. No randomness: the maze, start and goal are constants.

## Layout

Landscape 1280×720: the maze at left 30, top 48 with a 6px cyan `content-box` border; a 376px
panel on the right (padding 30/28, 12px gaps): title, hint, a 3×2 grid of move slots
(`direction: ltr` so moves read left to right in both languages), the repeat row, the status.
Portrait 720×1280: the maze at 24, 24 (660×495), the panel from `top: 560px`, 720×720,
padding 10/36/30. Switching is CSS on `[data-layout='portrait']`; the canvas is identical.

## Controls and states

Buttons are square (`border-radius: 0`), `min-height: 96px`, 4px solid borders, `#2a1f4a`.
A move slot is cyan, or muted `#5b4f86` when empty; tapping cycles
`none → up → right → down → left → none` through `NewLearnBoard.setVariables`. Repeat buttons
are yellow and fill solid yellow when `aria-pressed`. `#status` is a box with a 4px
`currentColor` border, coloured by `end` (green goal, pink wall, lavender otherwise). All
buttons are rebuilt each state. Highlight, reveal and notes are the helper's: a 4px `#e0a526`
outline, `[data-reveal]` (unused here) and a `#fff8e1` note at 32px.

## Motion

The reference does not animate: the robot appears at its end cell and the trail shows the
path, so a tap redraws at once and reduced motion is already the end picture. To step the
robot when the lesson moves on (`view.step` changed), move in whole tiles, draw the final
frame at once when `env.reducedMotion` is set, and end on exactly that frame.

## Do and don't

- Do keep one tiny canvas, integer tile sizes and a scale that fills the art area.
- Do draw sprites from string grids and a small named palette; keep 8×8, bright on dark.
- Do show the path or history (the trail) so the end picture explains what happened.
- Do give every outcome its own colour and sentence (goal, wall, short, empty), in HTML.
- Don't use rounded corners, shadows, gradients or smooth curves.
- Don't load sprite images, put words on the canvas, or use `Math.random` or time to draw.
- Don't draw sprites at fractional positions if you can avoid it: the reference's 1.5× robot
  lands on half pixels, which blurs once scaled; prefer whole-pixel scales.

## Before put_board

- `npm run board:check -- <folder>` passes: landscape and portrait, Arabic and English.
- Text ≥ 24px landscape and ≥ 32px portrait (hint and status are raised to 32 in portrait).
- Every button ≥ 88px on its short side (use 96); Tab reaches them when input is open.
- Same state ⇒ same frame: the logic is pure, the whole canvas is repainted each state.
- `image-rendering: pixelated` on the canvas, `libraries: []`, classic `<script src>` only.
